theme: Event-study and factor packages; earnings-surprise datasets; post-earnings-drift replication; Ken French factor loaders
queries_run: gh search repos "fama french factors python" --sort stars
gh search repos "event study python" --sort stars
gh search repos "earnings surprise dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "post earnings announcement drift" --sort stars
gh search repos "earnings surprise SUE" --sort stars
WebFetch raw READMEs for Jarod-Wingfield repo and riyadhmzyev event-study repo

candidates.name: Fama-French and Hou-Xue-Zhang Factors Replication
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed Factors_monthly.csv and Factor_sharpe_ratios.csv in /master: replicated Fama-French 6-factor and Hou-Xue-Zhang q-factor monthly series, 1971-2024 (per repo README, though authors note earlier years constrained by missing accounting data for q-factors). Built from CRSP/Compustat/CCM (WRDS) but output CSVs are committed and usable without WRDS access; also includes benchmark comparison files vs Ken French library and global-q.org.
candidates.why_useful: Extends what we already hold (plain Ken French 3/5-factor series) with q-factor model loadings and a longer monthly panel; useful as an alternative risk model for an ABNB earnings-day event study / CAR calculation, and a free cross-check against the Ken French numbers we already pull. Not a numbered gap but directly on-theme (Ken French factor loader + broader factor set).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps our existing Ken French factors holding but adds q-factors and a committed CSV rather than a live pull

candidates.name: Financial-Market-Event-Study-Python
candidates.what_it_holds: Reusable Python event-study framework: OLS market-model estimation, abnormal returns (AR) and cumulative abnormal returns (CAR), statistical significance testing, and visualization, built on historical price data (user-supplied, not bundled).
candidates.why_useful: Generic, reusable event-study package (not a one-off single-ticker notebook) that we could point at ABNB earnings dates plus the peer set (BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT) to measure abnormal-return reactions and drift; directly matches gap #17 (event-study packages, earnings-implied-move estimators).
candidates.size_hint: small Python repo, no bundled data

candidates.name: Empirical-Finance
candidates.what_it_holds: Combined toolkit: Fama-French model estimation, idiosyncratic volatility construction, and event-study code in one repo (per description); likely course-derived but multi-method rather than single-ticker.
candidates.why_useful: Same event-study + factor-loader combination as above, useful reference implementation for building an ABNB/peer earnings event study with risk adjustment.

candidates.name: getFamaFrenchFactors
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python package that pulls Fama-French factor files directly from the Kenneth French Data Library and returns a pandas DataFrame (one-command pull, no scraping of a hostile site).
candidates.why_useful: A clean, minimal one-command loader for the exact Ken French factors we already hold; useful only as a maintenance/automation convenience, not new data.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold Ken French factors; this is just a loader for the same public source

candidates.name: FamaFrenchData.jl
candidates.what_it_holds: Julia package providing programmatic access to the Ken French Data Library factor files.
candidates.why_useful: Same as getFamaFrenchFactors but in Julia; only relevant if the team ever needs a Julia pipeline.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Duplicate of Ken French factors we already hold

candidates.name: BR-Fama-French-Factors
candidates.what_it_holds: Open database of Fama-French style factors constructed for the Brazilian equity market (fills the stated absence of official FF factors for Brazil).
candidates.why_useful: Could support a Brazil-specific equity risk model if the team ever builds a LatAm-listed comparator regression, but is a factor dataset, not travel/STR/consumer data, so relevance to ABNB LatAm nights/ADR forecasting is indirect.

candidates.name: earnings-surprise-analysis (PEAD event study)
candidates.what_it_holds: PEAD/earnings-surprise event study described as covering 499 S&P 500 companies, 2015-2026, testing for increasing market efficiency; method and (likely) intermediate CAR/surprise output, not independently verified for committed raw data files.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying earnings-surprise series (SUE) are committed rather than WRDS-pulled, this would be a broad, recent (through 2026) cross-sectional earnings-surprise dataset relevant to gap #4 (historical consensus/surprise snapshots) and #17 (PEAD replication). Needs a closer look (not verified with directory listing) before relying on it.

candidates.name: pead-trading-system
candidates.what_it_holds: PEAD research/backtest/ML-signal system described as using "point-in-time data" and risk controls; not verified whether raw earnings-surprise or consensus data is committed vs pulled live from a paid vendor.
candidates.why_useful: Point-in-time discipline is exactly our rule #2; if it genuinely stores point-in-time consensus/earnings-surprise snapshots (rather than just point-in-time prices) it would be relevant to gap #4. Flagging for a closer look, not confirmed.

candidates.name: PEADReplication
candidates.what_it_holds: Academic-style replication and out-of-sample extension of Bernard & Thomas (1989) PEAD, with notebooks (notebooks_OOS, notebooks_sample), a write-up PDF, and papers/ folder; confirmed via directory listing that the committed data/ folder is empty (only a .DS_Store) — the pipeline is WRDS-dependent and ships no usable data.
candidates.why_useful: Well-documented replication methodology for PEAD if the team wants to reproduce SUE-decile drift tests, but contributes no free data of its own.

candidates.name: pead (SUE construction pipeline, R)
candidates.what_it_holds: An R pipeline to construct standardized earnings surprises (SUEs) for U.S. equities via WRDS.
candidates.why_useful: Reference methodology for building SUE series if the team ever gets WRDS/IBES access; ships no committed data itself.

candidates.name: FactorData
candidates.what_it_holds: Calculates 103 firm characteristics (factor zoo) directly from CRSP + Compustat in Python, avoiding the WRDS SAS cloud; no data committed, still requires paid WRDS access.
candidates.why_useful: Useful methodology reference for factor construction, but gated by paid data access we don't have; low direct value for the ABNB pitch.

candidates.name: quant-lab-alpha
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source investment analytics platform with Fama-French 5-factor portfolio risk decomposition, block-bootstrap Monte Carlo retirement modeling, max-drawdown/CVaR dashboards, Markowitz/Ledoit-Wolf optimisation, delivered as a UI tool rather than a dataset.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose factor/risk platform; could be repurposed to risk-decompose ABNB vs peers, but is tooling, not new data, and not earnings/event-study specific.

notes: Hard cap of 6 `gh search repos` calls was used exactly (fama french factors python [empty result — likely an API quirk with 3+ word phrase queries], event study python, fama-french, earnings surprise dataset [empty], post earnings announcement drift, earnings surprise SUE). WebSearch quota was exhausted session-wide before I could cross-check with a plain web search for the PyPI `eventstudy` package or academic PEAD replication archives (e.g. Zenodo-hosted IBES-derived SUE panels) — a future scout with WebSearch budget should try queries like 'eventstudy pypi github', 'IBES earnings surprise free dataset github', 'Zenodo post-earnings-announcement-drift replication data', and 'SEC EDGAR 8-K earnings surprise scraper github'. Overall finding for this theme: GitHub is saturated with near-identical student/course PEAD and Fama-French repos, almost none of which ship usable data — they assume paid WRDS/CRSP/Compustat/IBES access. The one genuine exception found is Jarod-Wingfield's repo, which commits actual monthly factor CSVs (FF6 + q-factors, 1971-2024) usable without WRDS. No repo found that fills gap #4 (point-in-time historical analyst-consensus/earnings-surprise snapshots) with committed free data — this remains an open gap. Two repos (dylan-jeon/earnings-surprise-analysis, AdityaAwe8/pead-trading-system) make claims worth a follow-up directory-listing check by the next scout on this theme, since I did not confirm whether their underlying data is committed or WRDS-pulled.
